title: Explicit knowledge of chief articles required — pure church-trust without grasp condemned
source_text: XLI. Nec etiam necesse putant ad fidem singulorum, ut explicite & distincte noverint quaecunque Dei Verbo traduntur atque continentur. Etenim absque multorum expressa notitia fatentur fidem consistere posse; nec ab omnibus eandem exigi cognitionis mensuram; sed ampliorem & distinctiorem cognitionem requiri in Ecclesiae Doctore, vel Pastore, quam in muliere, aut fideli privato. Verum hoc tantum volunt fidelibus omnibus, respectu praecipuorum fidei articulorum, necessariam esse expressam & explicatam aliquam notitiam. Neque veram esse posse & salutarem fidem illam, quae de articulis & dogmatis fidei nihil distincte apprehendit, sed confuse tantum credit quod credit Ecclesia; etsi plane nesciat quid Ecclesia credat, aut credere debeat. Qualis fides ab iis implicita vocatur, & damnatur eo nomine. Caeteroqui non negant ad fidem sufficere, si sigillatim & expresse noscantur & apprehendantur summa doctrinae salutaris capita, reliqua vero quae tradit Dei verbum, saltem generatim & confuse credantur.
pass_a_gloss: Nor do they think it necessary for the faith of individuals that they explicitly and distinctly know whatever things are handed down and contained in the Word of God. For they confess that faith can stand without express knowledge of many things; nor is the same measure of cognition required of all; but a fuller and more distinct cognition is required in a Doctor or Pastor of the Church than in a woman, or a private faithful person. Yet this alone they will have necessary for all the faithful, with respect to the chief articles of faith: some express and explicit knowledge. Nor can that faith be true and saving which distinctly apprehends nothing of the articles and dogmas of faith, but only confusedly believes what the Church believes — even if it plainly does not know what the Church believes, or ought to believe. Such faith is by them called implicit, and is condemned under that name. Otherwise they do not deny that it suffices for faith if the chief heads of saving doctrine are known and apprehended one by one and expressly, while the remaining things which the word of God hands down are at least believed generally and confusedly.
pass_b_english: Not every believer must distinctly know all Scripture contains.
Measure of knowledge differs — pastor/doctor more than a private believer.
All need some express explicit knowledge of the chief articles.
Blind church-trust with no distinct grasp of articles = condemned ‘implicit’ faith.
Enough: know the chief saving heads expressly; believe the rest at least in general.
